Normally, the user will simply copy and paste their API key.
Having an API key that does not comply with the format is
strange, even if in theory there is no possibility of bypassing
security. This may indicate that someone is trying to inject a
strange string in an attempt to bypass security. So let's not
refuse to validate the key here.

brute force attacks, and since the cache only temporarily
stores certain API keys and not all of them, I think it's
makes brute force attacks less effective; randomization
